physicalNotes: Radius 0.25247612 Jupiter radii from Peláez-Torres et al. 2024 (2024A&A...690A..62P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...690A..62P/abstract): 18,050 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0264 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Peláez-Torres et al. 2024 (2024A&A...690A..62P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PEL_AMP_AACUTE_EZ_TORRES_ET_AL__2024): P 4.07853 d
sources.shape: Peláez-Torres et al. 2024 (2024A&A...690A..62P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PEL_AMP_AACUTE_EZ_TORRES_ET_AL__2024): a/R* 22.46; Peláez-Torres et al. 2024 (2024A&A...690A..62P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PEL_AMP_AACUTE_EZ_TORRES_ET_AL__2024): inclination 89.25 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Peláez-Torres et al. 2024 (2024A&A...690A..62P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PEL_AMP_AACUTE_EZ_TORRES_ET_AL__2024): transit mid-time 2459496.5862 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 4 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
